newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek econmin sees inflation at 5.0 pct by summer.
newsitem.headline: Greek econmin sees inflation at 5.0 pct by summer.

text.p: Greece's National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou predicted that inflation would fall to 5.0 percent by summer and interest rates would drop to single-digits in the next few months.

Lower inflation would bolster real incomes and lead to lower lending rates for small and medium-size enterprises, business, industry and consumers, said Papandoniou who called inflation "the worker's worst enemy," in an interview with the daily Ethnos.
January CPI inflation stood at 6.8 percent year-on-year and the benchmark 12-month T-bill gross (before tax) interest rate at 10.9 percent.
There would be no new increases in the price of fuel but there would be "very small" increases in tariffs of public utilities later this year, he said.

"The fall in inflation means recovery and growth for the economy. Through investments there will be growth, there will be new jobs created, and Greece can break free of the vicious cycle of the last 20 years," said Papandoniou.
Papandoniou expressed concern about internal party dissent over economic policy that would put the government's hold on power at risk.

"PASOK (the ruling socialist party) has adjusted to new conditions. Today's PASOK under Costa Simitis... is different to the PASOK of Andreas Papandreou. 1997 is different from 1984 or 1981," said Papandoniou who stressed that 1997 would the most difficult year in the government's four-year mandate.
"1998 will again be difficult, but less difficult. In 1999 I believe that we will have taken off," Papandoniou told daily Ethnos. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
